title: When the Church disappoints
hook: scandal and failure are real and grievous
tomorrow: so why did Peter stay when others walked away?

segments.voice: This week was the parish from the inside: seven chosen to serve, a reader in Nazareth, Augustine at the hymns, a tired priest, Philip in the chariot, a cheerful giver. Yesterday's line: keep the doors open. Today, the hardest part.
screen: `KEEP THE DOORS OPEN.` → `THE PARISH FROM THE INSIDE.`

segments.voice: A gentle word first: today touches abuse in the Church, without details. Sometimes the headline is about your own: a name you recognize, a diocese you know, harm done by people meant to protect, and kept quiet for too long. What do you say? Scripture has words for this, and they aren't polite. Through the prophet Ezekiel, God says, in the Douay-Rheims Bible: "Woe to the shepherds of Israel, that fed themselves."
screen: `A HEADLINE ABOUT YOUR OWN.` → `KEPT QUIET TOO LONG.` → `WOE TO THE SHEPHERDS.`

segments.voice: Ezekiel goes on: the weak they did not strengthen, the lost they did not seek. Then God says he will seek the lost himself and bind up what was broken. Pope Francis wrote a letter to the whole Church owning this wound. He called the abuse crimes, said the Church had not cared for the little ones and had abandoned them, and asked every Catholic for penance and prayer. So the Church's own sources don't ask anyone to defend the indefensible, or to stop feeling it. They hand over lament instead, the psalm's cry: "How long, O Lord, wilt thou forget me unto the end?" Honest grief can stand right beside faith. And if any of this is your own story: it was not your fault, and you deserve to be believed. Tell someone you trust, or report it to the authorities. If you're in danger or thinking of harming yourself, call or text 988 in the US, or your local emergency number.
screen: `THE LOST THEY DID NOT SEEK.` · `A POPE NAMES THE CRIMES.` · `HOW LONG, O LORD?` · `IF IT'S YOUR STORY.` · then, large: `HONEST GRIEF.`

segments.voice: Take a pen and write one honest sentence about a way the Church, or any people of faith, have let you or someone you love down. Don't soften it. If you pray, you can read it to God the way the psalmist asked how long; if not, simply let it be said, and set the pen down.
When the Church disappoints. Facing real failure in the Church honestly, with grief that isn't hidden or explained away. Today's word.
Keep this one: honest grief, the kind the psalms already make room for. That's the week.

chat.says: mia sent me an article about church abuse cases. i didn't know what to say. defend it? leave?
options: Neither, first. Say it's wrong and it grieves you. Even the pope called it a crime.
Defend it. Those cases are old news, and bringing them up just hurts the Church.
Leave right away. If anyone failed like that, the whole faith must be fake.
chat.meaning: Ezekiel names shepherds who fed themselves, and Francis named the crimes. Honest grief doesn't defend the wrong or hide the pain.
